steps.body:
A quotient is a product in disguise: u/v = u·v⁻¹. Push that through the product rule and tidy up, and you get

**(u/v)′ = (u′v − uv′) / v²**.

The order matters now — the minus sign means **low·d-high minus high·d-low**, and swapping them flips the sign of the whole answer.

explanationVariants: The numerator collapses to 1, which is why this particular quotient is famously simple.

widget.prompt: f(x) = x/(x + 1). Find f′(1), as a decimal.

commonErrors.feedback: The sign is flipped — you subtracted in the wrong order. It is u′v − uv′ (low d-high minus high d-low), not the other way round.
That is f(1) = 1/2, the height. The slope is 1/(x+1)² = 1/4.
That is the numerator of the derivative before dividing by v² = 4.

steps.body: The minus sign, and where it comes from.

widget.prompt: Why a quotient has a minus and a square.

panels.title: Rewrite it
panels.body: u/v is u · v⁻¹. There is no new idea here — a quotient is a product with a negative power.

panels.title: Push it through
panels.body: The product rule gives u′·v⁻¹ + u·(−1)v⁻²·v′. The minus sign is not a convention someone chose: it falls out of differentiating v⁻¹.

panels.title: Tidy up
panels.body: Put both terms over v²: (u′v − uv′)/v². The square in the denominator is the v⁻² from the chain, and the minus is the −1 from the power rule. Every part of the rule has a reason.

widget.continueFeedback: Keep going — the minus sign is about to earn its place.
widget.successFeedback: The minus comes from differentiating v⁻¹, and the v² comes from the same place. Nothing was invented.

widget.prompt: f(x) = x²/(x + 1). Find f′(1), as a decimal.

commonErrors.feedback: Sign flipped: the order is u′v − uv′, which here is 2x(x+1) − x²(1), not the reverse.
That is f(1) = 1/2. The derivative is (x² + 2x)/(x+1)², which at 1 is 3/4.
You may have forgotten to divide by v² = (x+1)² = 4. The numerator alone is 3.

steps.body:
Two habits worth keeping.

**Simplify before you differentiate.** x³/x is just x². Reaching for the quotient rule there is legal but foolish.

**Never simplify the denominator away.** v² stays as it is — expanding it usually makes the answer harder to read and easier to get wrong.
Do you even need the rule?
explanationVariants: (x³ + x²)/x simplifies to x² + x, whose derivative is 2x + 1. At x = 2 that is 5.
The quotient rule would get the same answer with four times the work and four times the risk.

widget.prompt: f(x) = (x³ + x²)/x, for x ≠ 0. Find f′(2).

commonErrors.feedback: That is 2x at x = 2, missing the +1. Simplifying gives x² + x, so f′ = 2x + 1 = 5.
That looks like a quotient-rule slip. Simplify first: (x³ + x²)/x = x² + x.
That is 3x² at x = 2 — differentiating the numerator alone. Divide through by x first.

hints: (u/v)′ = (u′v − uv′)/v². You have all four values at x = 2.
explanationVariants: The rule needs only the four values — which is exactly why it is stated in u and v.

widget.prompt: u(2) = 6, u′(2) = 3, v(2) = 4, v′(2) = 1. Find (u/v)′(2), as a decimal to three places.

commonErrors.feedback: The subtraction ran the wrong way. It is u′v − uv′: 3(4) − 6(1) = 6, positive.
That is the numerator 6 divided by v = 4 instead of v² = 16.
That is 6/4 — the denominator must be SQUARED: 16.

steps.body: Low d-high minus high d-low, over low squared.
takeaways: (u/v)′ = (u′v − uv′)/v². The order of the subtraction decides the sign of the whole answer.
The minus and the square both fall out of differentiating v⁻¹ — nothing was invented.
Simplify first where you can: many quotients are powers in disguise.
steps.teaser: Next: pick the right rule, and combine them without panic.

concept.body: Write the four pieces down before you touch anything: u, u′, v, v′. Then assemble (u′v − uv′)/v² slowly. Almost every error in this chapter is a subtraction done in the wrong order.

explanationVariants: The numerator is u′v − uv′, so the DERIVATIVE OF THE TOP comes first.
Swapping the two terms negates the whole answer.

widget.prompt: Which is the correct numerator of (u/v)′?

options.label: u′v − uv′
options.feedback: Right — derivative of the top times the bottom, minus the top times the derivative of the bottom.

options.label: uv′ − u′v
options.feedback: That is the negative of the truth. The order of subtraction flips the sign of every answer you get.
